tagline: Down the barrier islands to a folk singer's park.
intro: A1A comes down out of Duval County through Ponte Vedra Beach and weaves through St. Augustine, the oldest continuously inhabited city on the mainland. For most of its 72 miles it is a two-lane road. Below Matanzas Inlet the old road washed out so often in storms that the highway was moved inland in the 1970s.

It ends at Flagler Beach in a park named for Gamble Rogers, a Florida folk singer and storyteller. He was camping there in 1991 when a girl ran to him for help with her father in the surf. He went in with an air mattress. Both men drowned.

moments.title: St. Augustine Light
moments.text: At the north end of Anastasia Island a working lighthouse from the 1870s keeps its original Fresnel lens, on a shore where the Spanish kept watchtowers and beacons from 1565.

moments.title: Fort Matanzas
moments.text: After Oglethorpe used Matanzas Inlet to lay siege to St. Augustine in 1740, the Spanish built this coquina watchtower to keep the back door shut.

moments.title: Marineland
moments.text: It opened in 1938 as Marine Studios, so Hollywood could film under water, and was incorporated as a town two years later. The 2020 census found 15 residents.
